title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference and Customer Requirements Library
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates customer requirements, reference architectures, packaging constraints, deployment checklists, day‑2 operational guidance, and upgrade/rollback procedures for Redwood Inference Private Deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for SREs, Solutions Engineers, and customer technical leads during scoping, delivery, and operations.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments delivered as: VPC-managed (customer VPC with private networking) and on‑prem packaged installs (air‑gapped or corporate datacenter).
- Covers pre‑sales requirements capture, deployment prerequisites, initial deployment steps, day‑2 operations, and upgrade/rollback playbooks.
- Does NOT cover hosted Redwood API usage or Dedicated multi‑tenant clusters.

1) High-level architecture overview
- Two supported modes:
  - VPC (recommended): Control plane hosted by Redwood with private peering (Transit Gateway / VPC peering) and data plane running in customer VPC.
  - On‑prem: Full control plane and data plane deployed inside customer network (air‑gap optional).

- Core components (packaged for both modes):
  - control-plane (operators, config API, auth integrations)
  - inference-fleet (GPU pool, autoscaler, runtime agents)
  - ops-daemon (prometheus exporters, agent for secret sync)
  - storage-backends (s3-compatible object store / NFS / Ceph for model artifacts)

2) Customer requirements library (quick reference table)
| Category | Minimum requirement | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Network | 1 Gbps dedicated links between inference nodes | 10 Gbps for production (multi‑GPU) | Latency < 2ms intra‑rack preferred |
| IPingress | Static egress IPs / NAT | Dedicated egress per cluster | Required for license callbacks and metrics |
| DNS | Customer DNS and internal names | Split‑horizon DNS for internal services | Avoid long TTLs during cutovers |
| K8s | v1.25+ (tested) | v1.26 in prod | Must support CRDs, Pod SecurityPolicies or OPA/Gatekeeper |
| GPUs | NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 | A30/A100 VGX for high throughput | Driver and CUDA versions pinned during onboarding |
| Storage | S3 compatible or NFS (POSIX) | S3 + local SSD cache on inference nodes | Model artifacts >100GB require object storage |
| Auth & KMS | Customer KMS (AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault recommended) | HSM for FIPS workloads | Key rotation procedures required for compliance |
| Compliance | SOC2/ISO evidence access | Enclave/air‑gap for high‑sensitivity | See security checklist below |

3) Pre‑deployment checklist (customer intake)
- Ownership and contacts: customer infra lead, security lead, networking lead, application owner.
- Network topology diagram and CIDR allocation.
- K8s cluster size, node types, GPU SKU list, node group autoscaling policy.
- Storage endpoints and credentials, object store bucket policy, encryption requirements.
- Certificate management approach (cert manager vs customer CA).
- Access model: SSO/SCIM integration, RBAC mapping.
- Compliance constraints: data residency, audit log retention, egress restrictions.

4) Packaging & on‑prem distribution
- Distribution format: Helm charts + operator manifests + tarball of OCI image mirrors (for air‑gapped).
- Packaging contents:
  - images.tar.gz (container images as OCI layout for local registry import)
  - manifests/ (Helm charts and kustomize overlays)
  - installers/ (bootstrap scripts for registry import and CSR signing)
  - checksums/ (sha256 for all artifacts)
  - packaging.json (release manifest: version, image digests, supported k8s versions)

- Supported customer registry workflows:
  1. Redwood pushes images to customer ECR/GCR/ACR — customer grants push perms (recommended).
  2. Customer imports images from artifacts bundle (air‑gapped).

Example packaging.json (excerpt):
{
  "release_version": "rdi-2027.03.1",
  "supported_k8s": "v1.25 - v1.27",
  "images": ["registry.local/rdi/control-plane:2027.03.1", "registry.local/rdi/inference-agent:2027.03.1"]
}

5) Deployment procedure (VPC mode, high level)
1. Validate pre‑reqs: CIDRs, peering, egress IPs, customer IAM role for S3 access.
2. Prepare customer infra: create EKS/GKE/AKS cluster or give access to existing cluster (ops role).
3. Register cluster with Redwood control plane (bootstrap token exchange over TLS).
4. Install base chart: rdi-base (CRDs, prometheus, cert-manager).
5. Install control-plane chart (operators, auth connectors).
6. Install inference-fleet (GPU node selectors, device plugin, local SSD caching).
7. Run smoke tests: model pull, inference call, metrics emitted.
8. Finalize: register SLOs with customer monitoring, handover runbooks.

Example CLI snippets (for air‑gapped import):
# Import images to local registry
ctr -n k8s.io images import images.tar.gz
# Apply Helm charts
helm upgrade --install rdi-base ./manifests/base --namespace rdi-system --create-namespace

6) Day‑2 operations (SRE playbook)
- Monitoring and alerting:
  - Metrics: request_latency_p50/95, tokens_per_second, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate.
  - Alerts (recommended thresholds):
    - GPU OOM rate > 0.5% over 15m -> Pager (oncall SRE)
    - request_latency_p95 > 3s for 5m -> Pager
    - control_plane_reconciliation_failures > 3 -> Channel (ops team)
- Log retention: default 30d; enterprise customers may require 365d as add‑on.
- Backups and disaster recovery:
  - Model artifact backups: object store lifecycle policy + immutability snapshots where required.
  - Etcd backup cadence: daily snapshot, hourly for high‑change clusters.
- Capacity planning:
  - Use historical qps and token per request to estimate GPU hours per month.
  - Autoscaler policy: target 60–75% GPU utilization for steady workloads.

7) Upgrade procedure (cluster component upgrades)
Preconditions:
- All smoke tests green for current release.
- Backup: etcd snapshot and object store sync completed within last 1 hour.
- Rollback plan documented and artifacts available.

Stepwise upgrade (canary -> progressive):
1. Create a canary namespace/cluster (1 node) and apply new release artifacts.
2. Run full smoke and perf tests against internal eval prompt sets (5–10 min).
3. If canary pass: rollout to 10% of inference-fleet nodes (node pool or deployment replicas) for 30–60 min.
4. Monitor key signals (latency, error rate, token output diffs).
5. If stable, proceed to 50% then 100% progressively, with 30–60 min observation windows.
6. If any stage fails, trigger rollback steps (see below).

Rollback procedure (fast stop):
1. Scale down new deployment and scale up previous replica set (Helm rollback or image revert).
2. Restore etcd snapshot if control plane corrupted (only if control-plane reconciliation fails irrecoverably).
3. Reopen incident channel and assign SRE lead.
4. Postmortem: capture root cause, impacted customers, lesson items.

8) Troubleshooting matrix (common signals -> first actions)
- Symptom: model pull fails
  - Check: object store credentials, bucket policy, network egress
  - Action: test aws s3 ls with cluster role; check proxy settings
- Symptom: GPU scheduling backlog
  - Check: device plugin logs, node allocatable, taints/tolerations
  - Action: add nodes to GPU nodepool, or reduce batch size temporarily
- Symptom: tokenization mismatch with canonical evals
  - Check: tokenizer version, model artifact digest
  - Action: revert model artifact to last-known-good digest, run regression evals

9) Security & compliance highlights (customer conversation checklist)
- Audit logging: event streams for model pulls, user operations, and admin actions (retention policy required).
- KMS integration: ensure keys never leave customer HSM where required.
- Network ACLs: deny internet egress from inference nodes except to approved object stores and Redwood control endpoints.
- Data residency: confirm model artifacts and telemetry storage locations.

10) Handover and runbook links
- On successful deployment, provide customer:
  - Operator runbook: restart sequence, config patching, key rotation steps.
  - Emergency rollback runbook (one‑page): top 5 commands to restore service.
  - Contact matrix: Redwood oncall -> solutions engineer -> customer infra lead.

Appendix A — Example emergency rollback one‑liner
# Helm rollback example (control-plane)
helm rollback rdi-control-plane 1 --namespace rdi-system

Appendix B — Supported binaries and versions
| Component | Minimum | Recommended |
| control-plane-operator | rdi-2026.11.0 | rdi-2027.03.1 |
| inference-agent | rdi-agent-0.9.2 | rdi-agent-1.2.0 |
